newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish debt office sees same '97 borrowing need.
newsitem.headline: Swedish debt office sees same '97 borrowing need.

text.p: Sweden's National Debt Office on Tuesday forecast an unchanged state borrowing need for 1997 at 20 to 30 billion crowns.
The office forecast the state would need to borrow five billion crowns in March.

The office also revised its February borrowing need forecast to -8.8 billion crowns from -9.8 billion. It said in January the borrowing requirement was 3.3 billion crowns compared to a forecast of 2.4 billion crowns one month ago.
It said in a statement it was continuing to issue relatively modest volumes of treasury bills and planned to issue 24 billion crowns worth in March as well as four billion crowns in bonds.
"The volumes are two billion crowns per issue, compared with six billion crowns just over a year ago," it said.
It said behind this decrease was the steady improvement in Sweden's state finances and extensive sales of index-linked bonds.
The office said in 1997 the net foreign currency borrowing will be close to zero but that it would refinance maturing capital market loans for some 50 billion crowns.
It also said it planned to reduce its short-term currency borrowing.
"Thanks to the favourable conditions on the international capital markets, the debt office has been able to make a very good start to this year's currency borrowing.
"The debt office has already raised approximately 35 percent of the gross foreign currency borrowing planned for the year," it said.
